docs.title: PyLoxone
docs.text:
PyLoxone is a Home Assistant integration for the Loxone Miniserver. It reads the Miniserver's structure file and maps each Loxone control to a Home Assistant entity.

  • Supported devices: which Loxone controls become which Home Assistant entities
  • Known limitations
  • Blueprints: ready-made automations and scripts

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
HACS (recommended)Manual
  1. Install HACS if you have not already.
  2. In HACS, open the menu → Custom repositories and add https://github.com/JoDehli/PyLoxone with the type Integration.
  3. Search for PyLoxone, install it and restart Home Assistant.
  4. Go to Settings → Devices & Services → Add Integration, search for PyLoxone and fill in the connection details.
  1. Download the latest release and extract it.
  2. Copy the custom_components/loxone folder into the custom_components folder next to your configuration.yaml.
  3. Restart Home Assistant.
  4. Go to Settings → Devices & Services → Add Integration, search for PyLoxone and fill in the connection details.

Requirements

Home Assistant 2025.2.4 or newer.

More setup details

The setup page covers the recorder configuration, the Gen 2 Miniserver and the cloud connection.

docs.title: Advanced usage and examples
docs.text: Ways to go beyond the supported entities: send websocket commands, use virtual inputs and build your own sensors.

docs.title: Websocket direct command service
docs.text:
If you want to send data directly to Loxone inputs or blocks that are not (yet) supported, you can use this service to send a command:

{
"uuid":"0f1e0b31-0179-7f77-ffff403fb0c34b9e",
"value":"pulse"
}
You can choose to send the commands using the UUID or the entity-name. See Developer Tools -> Services for more details. Websocket direct commands enable you to, for example, send data captured by devices integrated in Home Assistant immediately to the miniserver using a VI on the miniserver.

docs.title: Using a TextInput to control a block's API Connector
docs.text:
The TextInput Virtual Input in the Miniserver enables some neat advanced applications. The Audioserver for example, has limited API-support. If you want to switch presets from Home Assistant, this is not possible using the traditional Audio Player API interface.

A neat way around this, is by adressing the Audio Player block's API Connector using a VTI (Virtual Text Input). This enables all of the block's functionality in Home Assistant.

First, create a VTI and connect it to the block's API Connector.

Second, send anything you want to this VTI from Home Assistant. In this use case, we want the Audio Player to switch to preset 4:

service: loxone.event_websocket_command
data:
  value: SET(Ap;Fav;4)
  device: text.ingang_vti1
You can even directly address the Audio Player's TTS engine. 
service: loxone.event_websocket_command
data:
  device: text.ingang_vti1
  value: SET(AP;TTS;Woop-woop, that's the sound of da police)

docs.title: Using a Slider to send data from Home Assistant to the Loxone Miniserver
docs.text: The Miniserver connects to/interfaces with a wide range of third party devices and services. However, support is quite limited in comparison to Home Assistant. If you take the DSMR P1 digital meter interface for example. This (serial) interface is supported on a wide range of platforms, but not on the Miniserver. A workaround could be creating a VI on the Miniserver and configuring it as a Slider. This VI will then appear in this integration as a Number entity to which you can send any numerical value. Any change in the sensor value in Home Assistant should trigger an automation that sets the new value to the entity in the Loxone integration.

docs.title: Advanced usage: what to do if your device is not supported
docs.text: You can integrate nearly every Loxone Entity in your Home Assistant system by adding a custom sensor to your yaml file.

docs.title: Example 1 with a RoomComfortTemperature
docs.text:
Here is a example of a sensor which is displaying the comfort temperature of a room controller v2: 

sensor:
  - name: RoomComfortTemperature
    platform: loxone
    uuidAction: "15beed5b-01ab-d81d-ffff2b06d5b9c660"
    unit_of_measurement: "°C"
    device_class: "temperature"    # Use device classes from homeassitant for example temperature, humidity, voltage   
    state_class: "total"           # measurement, total or total_increasing see https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/sensor/#long-term-statistics
In this example a sensor with the name roomcomforttemperature (sensor.roomcomforttemperature) is created. The sensor is listening to all events from the loxone system with the specified uuid (How do you get the uuid?).

You can also send any websocket to a loxone entity for example to increase and decrease the temperature of a room controller v2. Here is a script that raises and lowers the temperature in 0.5 °C steps:

script:
  tempup:
    alias: TempUp
    mode: single
    sequence:
    - data_template:
        uuid: "15beed5b-01ab-d81f-ffff403fb0c34b9e" 
        value: "setComfortTemperature/{{ states('sensor.roomcomforttemperature')|float+0.5}}"
      service: loxone.event_websocket_command
  tempdown:
    alias: TempDown
    mode: single
    sequence:
    - data_template:
        uuid: "15beed5b-01ab-d81f-ffff403fb0c34b9e"
        value: "setComfortTemperature/{{ states('sensor.roomcomforttemperature')|float-0.5}}"
      service: loxone.event_websocket_command

docs.title: Example 2 with a UpDownAnalog
docs.text:
• First get the uuidAction as described above for example. Let's assume your uuidAction for the UpDownAnalog is 152ecfaa-03ac-f715-ffff403fb0c34b9e.
  • Create a Sensor do display the current value of the UpDownAnalog like this: 
    sensor:
  - name: "Up and Down Sensor"
    platform: loxone
    uuidAction: "152ecfaa-03ac-f715-ffff403fb0c34b9e"
    unit_of_measurement: ""
  • Create a script for incrementing up and down like this: 
    down:
  alias: Down
  mode: single
  sequence:
  - data_template:
      uuid: "152ecfaa-03ac-f715-ffff403fb0c34b9e"
      value: "{{ states('sensor.up_and_down_sensor')|float-1}}"
    service: loxone.event_websocket_command

up:
  alias: Up
  mode: single
  sequence:
  - data_template:
      uuid: "152ecfaa-03ac-f715-ffff403fb0c34b9e"
      value: "{{ states('sensor.up_and_down_sensor')|float+1}}"
    service: loxone.event_websocket_command

The commands for each entity can be found in the structure file. You can download it from the Loxone Homepage.

docs.title: How do you get the uuid?
docs.text:
If you need the UUID of an entity to use it in a service call or to manually add it to Home Assistant, you can get it from your Loxone setup by visit the following site with your prefered browser:

http://{ip-address-of-your-loxone}:{port}/data/LoxAPP3.json

{ip-address-of-your-loxone} --> replace with the ip of your loxone 

{port} --> replace with your port (default: 80)
After entering your username and password you will see your LoxApp3.json. You can paste it in your prefered JSON editor/viewer (eg. https://jsonformatter.org/). In this file you can find all your uuid ids for all your devices.

Here is a example of a Room Controller V2:

docs.title: Blueprints
docs.text:
This repository ships two Home Assistant blueprints for the Loxone integration. They live in blueprints/:

Blueprint Type File Purpose Loxone Message Center repair issue Automation blueprints/loxone_repair_issue.yaml Run your own actions when the Miniserver raises a new repair issue Loxone secured command Script blueprints/secured_command_input_helper.yaml Send a command to a secured Loxone control, asking for the visualisation password

docs.title: Installing a blueprint
docs.text:
Blueprints must be placed in the folder that matches their type. Home Assistant rejects a blueprint that sits in the wrong folder with an error such as Found incorrect blueprint type script, expected automation.

Go to Settings → Automations & Scenes → Blueprints → Import Blueprint and paste the URL for the blueprint you want:

  • Loxone Message Center repair issue (automation):
https://github.com/JoDehli/PyLoxone/blob/master/blueprints/loxone_repair_issue.yaml
  • Loxone secured command (script):
https://github.com/JoDehli/PyLoxone/blob/master/blueprints/secured_command_input_helper.yaml

The import dialog places each blueprint in the correct folder for its type. After importing, the blueprint appears when you create a new automation or script from a blueprint.

The secured command link only works after that file has been merged to master. Until then, it returns "not found".

docs.title: Loxone Message Center repair issue
docs.text: File: blueprints/loxone_repair_issue.yaml Type: automation

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
The Loxone integration reports problems from the Miniserver Message Center as repair issues (System Status). This blueprint runs whenever a new Loxone repair issue is created and then runs the actions you choose, for example:

  • a mobile notification
  • a TTS announcement
  • flashing a light

docs.title: Trigger and conditions
docs.text:
• Trigger: the Home Assistant event repairs_issue_registry_updated with action: create and domain: loxone. Only newly created issues start the automation. Updates and removals are ignored.
  • Condition: the issue severity must be at least the Minimum severity you chose.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Default Description Minimum severity warning Run the actions only for issues of this severity or higher. Options: Warning, Error, Critical. Actions — The actions to run for each new issue. Required.

docs.title: Variables for your actions
docs.text:
Use these variables in templates inside your actions:

Variable Content issue_id Unique id of the Message Center entry issue_title Title, plus the affected device name when known issue_message Description, including when the problem occurred issue_help_url Link to the Loxone help page (may be empty) issue_severity warning, error or critical issue_entry The raw Message Center entry sent by the Miniserver

docs.title: Example action
docs.text:
A mobile notification for each new issue:

action: notify.mobile_app_your_phone
data:
  title: "Loxone: {{ issue_title }}"
  message: "{{ issue_message }}"
  data:
    url: "{{ issue_help_url }}"

Replace notify.mobile_app_your_phone with your own notification service.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: • Mode: queued, with a maximum of 20 queued runs. If many issues arrive at once, they are processed one after another.

docs.title: Loxone secured command
docs.text: File: blueprints/secured_command_input_helper.yaml Type: script

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Sends a command to a secured Loxone control, such as a gate, door or alarm that requires the visualisation password. The script does not store the password. Whoever runs the script enters the password each time.

docs.title: Steps the script performs
docs.text:
1. Checks that a code was entered. If the code is empty or only spaces, the script stops with the error "No code was provided" and sends nothing.
  2. Calls the action loxone.event_secured_websocket_command with:
  3. device: the selected Loxone entity
  4. value: the command, as a string
  5. code: the password, with surrounding spaces removed

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Default Description Secured Loxone entity — The Loxone entity to control. Required. Command pulse Text sent to the control, for example pulse, on, off, open, close or delayedon/1.

docs.title: Field at run time
docs.text: Field Type Required Description Code Password text Yes The visualisation password for the control.

docs.title: Quick start: add it to the UI
docs.text:
1. Import the blueprint with the link above (Settings → Automations & Scenes → Blueprints → Import Blueprint).
  2. Go to Settings → Automations & Scenes → Scripts → Create script → Create from blueprint and select Loxone secured command.
  3. Choose the Loxone entity and enter the command (for example delayedon/1), then save.
  4. Open the script and choose Run script (German UI: Skript ausführen). Enter the visualisation password when asked.

Once saved, the script is an entity (for example script.loxone_secured_command). You can run it from the Scripts list, from the script's menu, or from a dashboard button with a password helper (see below).

docs.title: Creating the script
docs.text:
1. Go to Settings → Automations & Scenes → Scripts → Create script → Create from blueprint.
  2. Choose Loxone secured command.
  3. Select the Loxone entity and enter the command.
  4. Save. The script now appears under Scripts with its own entity id, such as script.loxone_secured_command.

docs.title: Running the script
docs.text:
• From the scripts list or the script's menu: choose Run script (German: Ausführen / Skript ausführen). Home Assistant asks for the code.
  • From a dashboard button: a button cannot ask for the code when tapped. Use a password helper instead (see below).

docs.title: Dashboard button with a password helper
docs.text:
1. Create a Text helper in Password mode, for example input_text.loxone_code.
  2. Add a Button card with this tap action, using your script's entity id:
type: button
name: Alarmanlage delayedon/1
tap_action:
  action: perform-action
  perform_action: script.loxone_secured_command
  data:
    command: delayedon/1
    code: "{{ states('input_text.loxone_code') }}"
  1. Type the code into the helper before tapping the button.

The helper keeps its value until you change it. Anyone who can use the dashboard can then run the command, so only do this on a dashboard you trust.

Security note: do not write the code directly into the button's YAML. The dashboard configuration is stored in plain text.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Cause and fix Invalid blueprint: Found incorrect blueprint type script, expected automation The script blueprint is in the automation folder. Move it to config/blueprints/script/. "No code was provided" The code field was empty or only spaces. Enter the password again. The button does nothing Check that the script entity id in the button matches your script, and that the helper contains the code.

docs.title: Intercom Gen 2
docs.text: Support for native local IntercomV2 devices.

docs.title: Entities
docs.text:
Native local IntercomV2 devices are discovered automatically. All entities of one Intercom are grouped on one device below the Miniserver:

Entity Purpose Ringing binary sensor The bell's ringing state, for dashboards and automations Mute doorbell switch Mutes/unmutes the Loxone bell; the state follows the Miniserver's feedback Dismiss ringing button Stops the bell without starting a conversation Output buttons Pulse the output subcontrols Loxone exposes, such as a door release Play reply buttons Play the voice replies configured in Loxone; each button shows its text as the message attribute Online binary sensor Whether the Intercom device is ready Device status sensor unknown, online, rebooting or initializing Firmware sensor Diagnostic entity, disabled by default; the firmware is also shown in the device information

Only the states and outputs Loxone exposes to the configured account become entities. An output pulse does not report whether a door is actually unlocked. PIN-protected (secured) Intercoms and outputs get no switch or button; use the loxone.event_secured_websocket_command action with the code instead. While a control is locked in Loxone, its switch and buttons are unavailable.

For a ringing notification, trigger on the Ringing sensor changing from off to on. Repeated presses while it is still ringing are not separate events.

Not supported yet: the camera with two-way audio, Intercoms of a trust member and custom IntercomV2 devices. This part was written without access to an Intercom Gen 2; the output buttons in particular are untested on hardware. Based on the work of jpulik in #542.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Pushbuttons are stateless. They cannot reliably trigger automations. Use a Switch as a workaround and turn it off again in the automation or in Loxone itself.
  • LightControllerV2 sub-controls are disabled by default. Enable them under Settings → Devices & Services → Entities, or turn on the integration option Generate sub-controls for LightControllerV2.
  • Partially supported controls (marked 🟡 on Supported devices) only offer a subset of the functions Loxone defines.
  • Intercom Gen 2 is experimental. It was written without access to an Intercom Gen 2 and the output buttons are untested on hardware. The camera, two-way audio, Intercoms of a trust member and custom IntercomV2 devices are not supported.
  • Not supported: LightController (V1), AlarmChain, AlarmClock.

docs.title: Message Center and repairs
docs.text: The Miniserver's Message Center (System Status) reports problems such as offline devices, low batteries or failed updates. The integration shows them as a sensor and as repair issues.

docs.title: Message Center (System Status)
docs.text: The Loxone Miniserver keeps a Message Center (shown as System Status in the Loxone app). It lists problems such as offline devices, low batteries, missing internet access or failed updates. The integration brings these messages into Home Assistant in two ways.

docs.title: The Message Center sensor
docs.text:
For each Message Center in your Loxone configuration, the integration creates a diagnostic sensor on the Miniserver device. Its entity id comes from the Loxone name, for example sensor.system_status. When the Miniserver reports a change, the integration fetches the current entries straight away.

  • State: the highest severity among the active entries:
State Meaning 0 No active messages 1 Info 2 Warning 3 Error 4 Critical
  • status attribute: the number of active entries for each severity, e.g. {2: 3, 3: 1} means three warnings and one error.

docs.title: Example: message templates
docs.text:
A template sensor that turns the numeric state into readable text:

template:
  - sensor:
      - name: Loxone System Status Text
        state: >-
          {% set level = states('sensor.system_status') | int(0) %}
          {{ {0: 'OK', 1: 'Info', 2: 'Warning', 3: 'Error', 4: 'Critical'}.get(level, 'Unknown') }}

A Markdown card that shows the entry counts and lists every active Loxone issue. It uses the status attribute and the issues() template function:

type: markdown
title: Loxone System Status
content: >-
  {% set counts = state_attr('sensor.system_status', 'status') or {} %}
  **{{ counts.get(4, 0) }}** critical, **{{ counts.get(3, 0) }}** errors, **{{ counts.get(2, 0) }}** warnings

  {% for key, item in issues().items() if key[0] == 'loxone' %}
  - **{{ item.translation_placeholders.title }}**{% if item.translation_placeholders.name %}: {{ item.translation_placeholders.name }}{% endif %} ({{ item.severity }})
  {% else %}
  No active Loxone issues.
  {% endfor %}

docs.title: Repairs
docs.text:
Each active Message Center entry also appears as a repair issue under Settings → System → Repairs, next to the repairs from any other integration. Each issue shows:

  • the Loxone title and the affected device;
  • the description and the time the problem occurred;
  • a link to the affected Home Assistant entity, when there is one;
  • a Learn more link to the Loxone help page, when Loxone provides one.

Loxone severities map to Home Assistant repair severities as follows: Info and Warning → warning, Error → error, Critical → critical. You can't fix these issues from Home Assistant. When an entry is resolved or acknowledged in Loxone, the repair issue is removed automatically.

docs.title: Example: automation for new repair issues
docs.text:
To do more than show the repair, react to the repairs_issue_registry_updated event. This example automation reads the new repair issue and creates a persistent notification for it:

alias: Notify on New Loxone Repair Issue
description: Sends a notification whenever a new repair issue is registered.
triggers:
  - event_type: repairs_issue_registry_updated
    trigger: event
    event_data:
      action: create
      domain: loxone
conditions: []
actions:
  - variables:
      title: >-
        {% set issue_item = issue(trigger.event.data.domain,
        trigger.event.data.issue_id) %}{{
        issue_item.translation_placeholders.title }}{% if
        issue_item.translation_placeholders.name %}: {{
        issue_item.translation_placeholders.name }}{% endif %}
      message: >-
        {% set issue_item = issue(trigger.event.data.domain,
        trigger.event.data.issue_id) %}{{
        issue_item.translation_placeholders.description }}
      help_link: >-
        {% set issue_item = issue(trigger.event.data.domain,
        trigger.event.data.issue_id) %}{% if issue_item.learn_more_url %}
        [Loxone Help]({{ issue_item.learn_more_url }}){% endif %}
  - data:
      title: '{{ title }}'
      message: |-
        {{ message }}
        {{ help_link }}
      data:
        notification_id: '{{ trigger.event.data.issue_id }}'
    action: notify.persistent_notification

docs.title: Blueprints
docs.text: The repository ships an automation blueprint that runs your own actions for new repair issues. See the Blueprints page for import instructions.

docs.title: Blueprint: run your own actions for new repair issues
docs.text:
The repository includes an automation blueprint, blueprints/loxone_repair_issue.yaml. It triggers on every new Loxone repair issue and runs the actions you choose, such as a mobile notification, a TTS announcement or flashing a light. You can also set a minimum severity so that only errors or critical issues run your actions.

You can also import it manually: go to Settings → Automations & Scenes → Blueprints → Import Blueprint and paste this URL:

https://github.com/JoDehli/PyLoxone/blob/master/blueprints/loxone_repair_issue.yaml

Your actions can use these variables in templates:

Variable Content issue_id Unique id of the Message Center entry issue_title Title, plus the affected device name when known issue_message Description, including when the problem occurred issue_help_url Link to the Loxone help page (may be empty) issue_severity warning, error or critical issue_entry The raw Message Center entry from the Miniserver

For example, to send a notification to your phone:

action: notify.mobile_app_my_phone
data:
  title: "{{ issue_title }}"
  message: "{{ issue_message }}"
  data:
    url: "{{ issue_help_url }}"

docs.title: Sensors
docs.text: How the integration decides the device class of a sensor and how to override it.

docs.title: Sensor Device Class Detection
docs.text:
Sensors (InfoOnlyAnalog, Meter) are automatically classified based on their unit and Loxone category/name. The following device classes are detected:

Device class Detected by temperature Unit: °C, °F humidity Unit: % and category or name contains "humidity", "vlhkost", "feucht", or "humidité" battery Unit: % and name contains "batt", "akku", or "battery" energy Unit: kWh, Wh, MWh power Unit: W, kW volume_flow_rate Unit: L/h, L/min water Unit: L illuminance Unit: lx, Lx, lux carbon_dioxide Unit: ppm wind_speed Unit: km/h

Sensors with % unit that don't match any keyword are left without a device class.

docs.title: Overriding the detected device class
docs.text:
If the automatic detection assigns the wrong device class (or you want to set one for an unclassified sensor), use Home Assistant's built-in entity customization in configuration.yaml:

homeassistant:
  customize:
    sensor.my_percentage_sensor:
      device_class: battery
  customize_glob:
    sensor.*humidity*:
      device_class: humidity

docs.title: Setup and configuration
docs.text: Add the recorder exclusion before you use the integration, then choose a local or cloud connection.

docs.title: Recorder configuration (important)
docs.text:
Add this before you use the integration

A Loxone system generates a few thousand events per day. Without this exclusion, Home Assistant records all of them and the database can grow very quickly. Add it to your configuration.yaml.

recorder:
  exclude:
    event_types:
      - loxone_event

docs.title: Config for the gen2 miniserver
docs.text: If you have the gen2 miniserver you should connect via local access. It is more reliable and faster than a cloud connection.

docs.title: Config for cloud connection
docs.text:
Please use this only in case local access is not possible.

Example: - Miniserver Ip: https://dns.loxonecloud.com/123456789ABC - Port: 443

Change 123456789ABC to your miniserver Serial Number.

docs.title: LightControllerV2 Sub-Controls
docs.text:
Each LightControllerV2 in Loxone groups individual lighting outputs (dimmers, color pickers, switches) as sub-controls. These are registered in the Home Assistant entity registry but disabled by default to keep the UI clean.

To access individual light outputs:

  1. Open Settings → Devices & Services → Entities
  2. Filter by your LightControllerV2 device
  3. Enable the sub-control entities you want to use (dimmer, color picker, etc.)

The integration option "Generate sub-controls for LightControllerV2" controls the default enabled state for newly created sub-control entities. When enabled, new sub-controls start as enabled; when disabled (the default), they start as disabled but remain visible in the entity registry for manual activation.

docs.title: Log Configuration
docs.text:
Use the following settings if you paste a log into a issue:

logger:
  default: warning
  logs:
    homeassistant: warning
    homeassistant.helpers: warning
    custom_components.loxone: debug
    pyloxone_api.connection: debug

The Loxone communication lives in the pyloxone-api package, which is a separate package (logger name pyloxone_api, not custom_components.loxone). Use pyloxone_api.connection: debug to see the login steps (authwithtoken, gettoken, ...).

docs.title: Token storage
docs.text:
After a successful login the integration saves the Loxone token in its config entry (.storage/core.config_entries in your Home Assistant config folder). The token is bound to the host, port and user of the entry. It is used for later starts so that no password login is needed. A token for a different host, port or user is ignored.

  • After updating from an older version, the first start performs one password login. This is expected.
  • Treat the .storage folder as sensitive: the stored token logs in as your Loxone user.
  • Removing the integration tries to invalidate the token on the Miniserver. This only works while the connection is still open; otherwise the token expires on its own.

docs.title: Supported devices
docs.text:
This page lists the Loxone control types and the Home Assistant entities they become.

Status Meaning ✅ Supported Works as described by the Loxone documentation 🟡 Partial Works for the common use cases; some functions are missing (see Notes) ❌ Not supported No entity is created

If your control is missing or only partly supported, please open a feature request.

docs.title: Lighting
docs.text: Loxone control Home Assistant Status Notes LightControllerV2 light, switch 🟡 Partial Moods are exposed as light effects, plus master brightness. Sub-controls (dimmers, color pickers, switches) are created but disabled by default. Favorite and additional moods are not used. Dimmer, EIBDimmer light ✅ Supported ColorPickerV2 light 🟡 Partial HSV and color temperature work as a sub-control. Sequences and favorites are missing. The old ColorPicker is not supported. LightController (V1) – ❌ Not supported

docs.title: Blinds, windows and gates
docs.text: Loxone control Home Assistant Status Notes Jalousie cover ✅ Supported Window cover ✅ Supported Includes the partially open (ventilation) position as the loxone.window_slightly_open service. Gate cover ✅ Supported WindowMonitor binary_sensor, sensor ✅ Supported

docs.title: Switches and inputs
docs.text: Loxone control Home Assistant Status Notes Switch switch ✅ Supported TimedSwitch switch ✅ Supported Turning on sends a pulse. Pushbutton button ✅ Supported Buttons are stateless, see Known limitations. Slider number ✅ Supported ValueSelector number ✅ Supported TextInput text, sensor ✅ Supported Radio select ✅ Supported A locked radio block rejects selections.

docs.title: Sensors
docs.text: Loxone control Home Assistant Status Notes InfoOnlyAnalog sensor ✅ Supported Device class is detected from the unit, see Sensors. InfoOnlyDigital binary_sensor ✅ Supported Shows unknown until the first value arrives. InfoOnlyText sensor ✅ Supported Also text memory flags once "Use" is ticked in Loxone Config. TextState sensor ✅ Supported Read-only. State is limited to 255 characters; the full text is in the text attribute. Meter sensor ✅ Supported PresenceDetector binary_sensor ✅ Supported SmokeAlarm binary_sensor ✅ Supported Read-only; mute and confirm commands are not available.

docs.title: Climate and ventilation
docs.text: Loxone control Home Assistant Status Notes IRoomControllerV2 climate, switch, sensor 🟡 Partial IRoomController climate 🟡 Partial Timer commands are missing. AcControl climate 🟡 Partial ClimateController, ClimateControllerUS sensor 🟡 Partial Only the heating/cooling demand is exposed. Ventilation fan 🟡 Partial Speed and presets plus presence, humidity and air-quality sensors.

docs.title: Security, audio and intercom
docs.text: Loxone control Home Assistant Status Notes Alarm alarm_control_panel ✅ Supported AudioZoneV2 media_player 🟡 Partial Play, pause, next, previous and volume. Text-to-speech, favorites and presence are missing. Intercom switch 🟡 Partial Sub-controls appear as switches; the doorbell is not visible. IntercomV2 (Gen 2) binary_sensor, switch, button, sensor, text 🟡 Partial Experimental. Ringing, bell mute, dismiss, outputs, voice replies and diagnostics. No camera or two-way audio yet. Secured Intercoms and outputs get no entities. Output buttons are untested on hardware. See Intercom Gen 2.

docs.title: Other
docs.text: Loxone control Home Assistant Status Notes Message Center / System Status sensor, repairs ✅ Supported See Message Center and repairs and the blueprints. AlarmChain, AlarmClock – ❌ Not supported

docs.title: Energy
docs.text:
Loxone control Home Assistant Status Notes Wallbox2 (Wallbox Gen. 2) switch, select, number, binary_sensor ✅ Supported Charging allow switch, charging mode, manual charging limit in kW, and connected / charging / load shedding / phase switching sensors. The kW range was verified on an 11 kW Wallbox Gen. 2 only.

Unsupported control?

You can still send commands to any control with the websocket direct command service. See Advanced usage.

docs.title: Developer guide
docs.text: PyLoxone is a Home Assistant custom integration. The code lives in custom_components/loxone/; the connection to the Miniserver is handled by the separate pyloxone-api package, which is pinned in requirements.txt.

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text: Path Content custom_components/loxone/ The integration: one file per Home Assistant platform (light.py, cover.py, climate.py, …), config_flow.py, miniserver.py, coordinator.py. intercom/ (Intercom Gen 2) and wallbox2.py (Wallbox Gen 2) are feature packages that feed several platforms tests/ Offline test suite; runs the integration inside the Home Assistant test harness against tests/fixtures/LoxAPP3.json, no Miniserver needed blueprints/ Home Assistant blueprints shipped with the integration config/ Home Assistant configuration used by the dev container (git-ignored except configuration.yaml) scripts/ Helper scripts, see below docs/ Internal notes site-docs/ Source of this documentation site

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: The recommended setup is the dev container. It contains Python 3.14, all dependencies and a Home Assistant instance that loads the integration from this repository.

docs.title: Scripts
docs.text: Script Purpose scripts/setup Installs system packages and dependencies, links the integration into config/; runs automatically when the dev container is created scripts/test Runs the test suite in its own virtualenv .venv-test scripts/lint Formats the code with ruff format scripts/docs Live preview of this documentation

docs.title: Running the tests
docs.text:
./scripts/test                                  # whole suite
./scripts/test -q                               # quiet
./scripts/test tests/test_light_commands.py -x  # one file, stop at first failure

The test virtualenv is created on first use. It is separate from .venv on purpose: the test requirements pin a specific Home Assistant version.

docs.title: Working on the documentation
docs.text:
./scripts/docs            # live preview on http://127.0.0.1:8000/PyLoxone/
./scripts/docs --build    # strict build, fails on broken links

Pages are Markdown files in site-docs/; the navigation is defined in mkdocs.yml. Pushes to master that touch the docs are published to GitHub Pages by the Docs workflow.

Note

site-docs/blueprints.md is generated from BLUEPRINTS.md and site-docs/developer/devcontainer.md and connection-flow.md are copies of docs/DEVCONTAINER.md and docs/CONNECTION_FLOW.md. implemented-control-types.md is maintained by hand and condensed from docs/IMPLEMENTED_CONTROL_TYPES_EN.md. Update the originals and copy the changes over.

docs.title: Further reading
docs.text:
• pyloxone-api: the library that talks to the Miniserver, versioning and local development
  • Loxone Structure File (Loxone): format of LoxAPP3.json and the control types, the basis for the entity mapping
  • Implemented control types: current state per control type and the gaps that are still open
  • Connection flow: HTTP bootstrap → WebSocket → authentication → operation → reconnect

docs.title: Loxone Miniserver – Connection Flow (Connect)
docs.text: Source: Communicating with the Miniserver (Loxone) and pyloxone_api (src/pyloxone_api/connection.py im Paket-Repo).

docs.title: Quick overview
docs.text:
1. HTTP bootstrap (open()): check reachability, load the structure file + public key, RSA-encrypt the AES session key, open the WebSocket.
  2. WebSocket authentication (start_listening() / _websocket_event()): key exchange → getkey2 → token auth or token acquisition → enable updates.
  3. Operation: receive loop, keepalive (30 s), token refresh, encrypted/secured commands.
  4. Supervision (run()): reconnect/backoff, escalation on auth errors.

docs.title: Phase 0 – Preparation (constructor)
docs.text:
• Parse host/port/scheme, normalize the URL.
  • Generate the AES-256-CBC key (_aes_key, 32 bytes) and IV (_iv, 16 bytes) per instance.
  • Take over an existing token cache if present.
  • Create the message queue, salt state and visual-hash state.

docs.title: Phase 1 – HTTP bootstrap (open())
docs.text:
With bounded exponential backoff (_get_with_retry, 5 attempts):

  1. GET /jdev/cfg/apiKey → version, SNR, local.
  2. If local == false, adjust the URL via Cloud-DNS redirect (_apply_url).
  3. GET /data/LoxAPP3.json → structure file into structure_file.
  4. GET /jdev/sys/getPublicKey → certificate → RSA public key.
  5. Build the session key: encrypt the payload "{aes_key_hex}:{iv_hex}" with RSA PKCS#1 v1.5, Base64 → _session_key.
  6. Generate the salt (_generate_salt).

docs.title: Phase 2 – Open WebSocket
docs.text:
• URL ws(s)://{host}/ws/rfc6455 (build_loxone_url), subprotocol remotecontrol.
  • ping_interval=None (the Loxone keepalive is the liveness channel).

docs.title: Phase 3 – Authentication
docs.text:
1. Immediately after connect: jdev/sys/keyexchange/{session_key}.
  2. Response keyexchange → sends jdev/sys/getkey2/{encoded_username}.
  3. From the response: key, salt, hashAlg.

Branching:

  • Token still valid (> 100 s remaining lifetime): hash over the token → authwithtoken/{token_hash}/{user}.
  • Token missing/expired: password hash → jdev/sys/gettoken/{hash}/... (or getjwt from FW 10.2). The response provides token, validUntil, key.

Completion: _authenticated_event.set(), token-change callback, jdev/sps/enablebinstatusupdate.

docs.title: Phase 4 – Operation
docs.text:
• Receive loop: parses the binary Loxone protocol (8-byte header + body, chunking/estimated length), dispatches to _websocket_event() and the HA callback.
  • Keepalive: every 30 s (KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD) keepalive; watchdog after 90 s without an incoming frame.
  • Token refresh: after auth, wait ~50 % of the remaining lifetime, then async_refresh_token; escalate after 10 failed attempts.
  • Reconnect task: on a reconnect event, LoxoneTokenError is raised.
  • Secured commands: stash in _secured_queue, jdev/sys/getvisusalt/{user}, then send the HMAC command.

docs.title: Phase 5 – Supervision (run())
docs.text:
• Loop over open()/start_listening().
  • Retryable errors → close(), backoff ±20 % jitter, retry.
  • Auth errors → pass on to the integration (delete token / reload).
  • close() sets the shutdown event and terminates.

docs.title: Flow diagram
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant HA as Home Assistant / Coordinator
    participant C as LoxoneConnection
    participant HTTP as Miniserver (HTTP)
    participant WS as Miniserver (WebSocket)

    HA->>C: run() / start_listening()

    note over C,HTTP: Phase 1 – HTTP bootstrap (open())
    C->>HTTP: GET /jdev/cfg/apiKey
    HTTP-->>C: version, snr, local
    opt not local
        C->>C: adjust URL via Cloud-DNS redirect
    end
    C->>HTTP: GET /data/LoxAPP3.json
    HTTP-->>C: structure file
    C->>HTTP: GET /jdev/sys/getPublicKey
    HTTP-->>C: certificate → RSA public key
    C->>C: encrypt AES key:iv with RSA
    C->>C: generate salt

    note over C,WS: Phase 2 – WebSocket
    C->>WS: ws(s)://host/ws/rfc6455 (remotecontrol)
    WS-->>C: connection open

    note over C,WS: Phase 3 – Auth
    C->>WS: jdev/sys/keyexchange/{session_key}
    WS-->>C: keyexchange
    C->>WS: jdev/sys/getkey2/{user}
    WS-->>C: key, salt, hashAlg

    alt token still valid (>100s)
        C->>WS: authwithtoken/{token_hash}/{user}
    else re-authenticate
        C->>C: build password hash
        C->>WS: jdev/sys/gettoken/{hash}/... (or getjwt)
        WS-->>C: token, validUntil, key
    end
    C->>WS: jdev/sps/enablebinstatusupdate
    C->>C: set _authenticated_event

    note over C,WS: Phase 4 – Operation
    par receive loop
        WS-->>C: status/text messages
    and keepalive (30s)
        C->>WS: keepalive
    and token refresh
        C->>WS: refreshjwt (after ~50% lifetime)
    end

    note over HA,C: On drop: run() → close() → backoff → retry

docs.title: Error codes (from the docs)
docs.text:
• 401 / 4003: unauthorized / too many failed attempts (close 4003).
  • 420: not authenticated within the first seconds.
  • 400: another command before auth.
  • Further CloudDNS codes see the docs (403, 405, 409, 412, 418, 481–483).

docs.title: Dev container
docs.text: The dev container (.devcontainer.json) is the supported way to develop and debug this integration. It contains Python 3.14, the project's dependencies and Home Assistant, which runs on port 8123 and loads the Loxone integration from this repository.

docs.title: What happens when the container is created
docs.text:
• The image is mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/python:3.14. It matches .python-version and requires-python >=3.14.2.
  • postCreateCommand runs scripts/setup, which:
  • installs the system packages ffmpeg, libturbojpeg0 and libpcap-dev with sudo apt-get (Home Assistant needs them for its ffmpeg and camera integrations). They are not a devcontainer feature, because the feature failed to build under Podman,
  • installs requirements.txt and requirements-dev.txt,
  • installs requirements-ha-integrations.txt, the pinned packages of the Home Assistant integrations that default_config loads,
  • links config/custom_components to custom_components/ (skipped if it already exists), because Home Assistant only loads custom integrations from there,
  • runs hass --script ensure_config.
  • Format on save and on paste are off. Formatting would rewrite lines in open PRs. See the TODO in .pre-commit-config.yaml.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: You need a container engine. Docker is not required on Linux.

docs.title: Linux
docs.text:
• Docker or Podman. Podman works with the devcontainer CLI and with VS Code, see below.
  • For Podman with rootless storage on ext4, install fuse-overlayfs:
sudo pacman -S fuse-overlayfs        # Arch; use your distro's package manager
mkdir -p ~/.config/containers
cat > ~/.config/containers/storage.conf <<'EOF'
[storage]
driver = "overlay"

[storage.options.overlay]
mount_program = "/usr/bin/fuse-overlayfs"
EOF
podman info --format '{{.Store.GraphDriverName}}'   # should print: overlay

Without it you get kernel does not support overlay fs.

  • For Podman the TUN module must be available for the running kernel. If the build fails with pasta failed ... /dev/net/tun: No such device, the running kernel and its modules do not match. This happens after a kernel update without a reboot. Reboot, then check with uname -r and sudo modprobe tun.

docs.title: macOS and Windows (not tested by the maintainer)
docs.text:
• Docker Desktop (on Windows with the WSL 2 backend), or Podman Desktop.
  • Docker Desktop must be running before you reopen the project in the container.

The steps below are written for Linux. The VS Code steps should be the same on macOS and Windows, but that is not verified yet. One known risk on Windows: the config/custom_components link is created inside the container, and Git on Windows can check out symlinks as plain text files. The link is git-ignored, so it is only a local artefact, but check it if Home Assistant does not find the integration.

docs.title: VS Code
docs.text:
1. Open the repository in VS Code.
  2. Ctrl+Shift+P (Cmd+Shift+P on macOS) → Dev Containers: Reopen in Container. After changes to .devcontainer.json use Rebuild Container.
  3. Wait until the post-create step has finished. Check the output in the "Dev Containers" channel of the Output panel.

docs.title: Podman as the engine in VS Code
docs.text:
Set this in your user settings, not in the repository, because the path to Podman differs between machines:

"dev.containers.dockerPath": "podman"

If VS Code reports Docker version 17.12.0 or later required, it looks for a docker command. Install the shim package (podman-docker on Arch) and restart VS Code completely. Do not click Install in that dialog, it tries to install Docker.

docs.title: Command line (devcontainer CLI)
docs.text:
npm install -g @devcontainers/cli
cd <repo>
devcontainer up --workspace-folder . --docker-path podman   # or: docker
devcontainer exec --workspace-folder . --docker-path podman python3 --version

The second command should print Python 3.14.x.

docs.title: Running and debugging Home Assistant
docs.text:
1. In VS Code open Run and Debug (Ctrl+Shift+D).
  2. Choose Home Assistant and press F5. This is the configuration in .vscode/launch.json. It runs python -m homeassistant --debug -c config.
  3. Open http://localhost:8123. The first start shows the onboarding page, where you create a user.
  4. Add the integration in Settings → Devices & services → Add integration → Loxone.

Breakpoints in custom_components/loxone/ are hit only if the integration is loaded, which is what the config/custom_components link is for.

Expected log output: the warning We found a custom integration loxone which has not been tested by Home Assistant is normal. go2rtc is not loaded (see config/configuration.yaml), and default_config is replaced by the same list of integrations without it, because go2rtc needs a Docker binary inside the container.

docs.title: Discovery is off in the dev container
docs.text:
The discovery integrations bluetooth, dhcp, ssdp, usb and zeroconf are removed from config/configuration.yaml. The Loxone integration does not use them. Discovery scans the network and starts integrations whose requirements are not installed in the container, which produced No module named ... errors (for example psnawp_api for playstation_network).

If you need discovery, add the integration back to config/configuration.yaml yourself. Its Python packages are not in requirements-ha-integrations.txt. Copy the pins from the integration's manifest.json (requirements entry) for the Home Assistant version in requirements-dev.txt, then install them in the container. Until then, the integration logs No module named ....

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
From the container terminal:

pytest -q

docs.title: Notes on the repository state
docs.text:
• config/ is git-ignored except configuration.yaml. Home Assistant writes its state (.storage/, logs, database) there at runtime. Do not commit those.
  • Never run Home Assistant as root in the container. Files written as root end up owned by a different user on the host, and Home Assistant then cannot write to them as vscode. If that happens, remove the affected files with a throwaway container or from a root shell.
  • A local .venv on the host is not needed for the container workflow.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix kernel does not support overlay fs Podman has no rootless overlay storage Install fuse-overlayfs, see above pasta failed ... /dev/net/tun: No such device Running kernel and modules do not match Reboot after kernel updates Docker version 17.12.0 or later required VS Code looks for docker Set dockerPath to podman, install podman-docker No module named 'hass_frontend' (and similar) Post-create step did not finish Rebuild the container, or run bash scripts/setup in the container terminal Permission denied on config/.storage/... Files written as root in config/ Remove the affected files, see above ffmpeg / libturbojpeg / libpcap errors in the log System packages missing Run sudo apt-get install -y ffmpeg libturbojpeg0 libpcap-dev in the container terminal, or run bash scripts/setup again go2rtc errors Needs a Docker binary Expected; go2rtc is excluded from config/configuration.yaml

docs.title: Implemented control types
docs.text:
Current state of the Loxone control types from the Loxone Structure File in the integration: which file handles them and what is still missing. The user-facing summary is on Supported devices. All files are in custom_components/loxone/.

Status: implemented = covers the Structure File spec, partial = works, with the gaps listed, missing = no entity.

docs.title: Lighting
docs.text: Control type File Status Open gaps LightControllerV2 light.py, switch.py partial Moods as effects, master brightness, on/off from moods and master value. favoriteMoods / additionalMoods unused; mood-maintenance commands missing Dimmer, EIBDimmer light.py implemented Cosmetic only: no min/max/step attributes ColorPickerV2 (also ColorPicker) light.py (sub-control) partial HSV and color temperature work. Sequences and favorites missing; V1 ColorPicker unsupported LightController – missing

docs.title: Blinds, windows, gates
docs.text: Control type File Status Open gaps Jalousie cover.py implemented Commands up/UpOff, down/DownOff, manualPosBlind, setAdjustingEndPos, endPosAdjustment not used Window cover.py implemented Commands open/on, open/off, close/on, close/off not used. slightlyOpen/ is exposed as the service loxone.window_slightly_open; lockedReason and the window type are read as attributes Gate cover.py implemented Commands forceOpen, forceClose, PartiallyOpen, getState, stop not used WindowMonitor window_monitor.py → binary_sensor.py, sensor.py implemented

docs.title: Switches and inputs
docs.text: Control type File Status Open gaps Switch switch.py implemented States lockedOn, jLocked not used TimedSwitch switch.py implemented turn_on only sends pulse; the permanent on command is missing Pushbutton button.py implemented Only pulse; on / off missing Slider number.py implemented States error, jLocked not used ValueSelector number.py implemented States increaseOnly, jLocked not used TextInput sensor.py, text.py implemented jLocked and limits not used Radio select.py implemented jLocked is decoded and a locked block rejects selections. Commands next / prev missing

docs.title: Sensors
docs.text: Control type File Status Open gaps InfoOnlyAnalog sensor.py implemented State error not used. The JSON sometimes uses the type name analog InfoOnlyDigital binary_sensor.py implemented text / image / color not used. The JSON sometimes uses the type name digital. Reports unknown until the first event InfoOnlyText sensor.py implemented details.format ignored; no 255-character cap TextState sensor.py implemented Read-only. State capped at 255 characters, full text in the text attribute. textAndIcon is treated as plain text and not yet verified against a live event Meter sensor.py implemented totalDay / totalWeek / …, displayType, powerName, storageMax and the reset command missing PresenceDetector binary_sensor.py implemented Commands {value}, time/{value}, presence/{value}, deactivate/{value} missing SmokeAlarm binary_sensor.py implemented Alarm state from level. Commands mute, confirm, servicemode/{number}, startDrill missing

docs.title: Climate and ventilation
docs.text: Control type File Status Open gaps IRoomControllerV2 climate.py, switch.py, sensor.py partial setComfortModeTemp sends the offset. setecoplus* commands are undocumented but accepted by the Miniserver IRoomController climate.py partial Timer commands, stop / error / manualMode missing; undocumented valve/prepare states to verify AcControl climate.py partial Direct state access, minTemp / maxTemp ignored, stray setMode on power-off; no real instance tested ClimateController, ClimateControllerUS sensor.py partial Only the request/demand relay. The mode numbering differs between the two types Ventilation fan.py partial Speed and presets plus presence, humidity and air-quality sub-sensors. setMode/2..6 is undocumented and the preset ids are hardcoded

docs.title: Energy
docs.text: Control type File Status Open gaps Wallbox2 (Wallbox Gen. 2) wallbox2.py → switch.py, select.py, number.py, binary_sensor.py implemented Commands allow/on, allow/off, setmode/<id>, manualLimit/<kW>. min/max are assumed to be kW and verified only on an 11 kW Wallbox Gen. 2

docs.title: Security, audio, intercom
docs.text: Control type File Status Open gaps Alarm alarm_control_panel.py implemented AudioZoneV2 media_player.py partial Transport only (play, pause, next, previous, volume, step; stop maps to pause). Missing: tts, favorites, presence/bluetooth, availability from serverState. Zones with volumeModes: 2 get wrong absolute-volume commands Intercom switch.py partial V1 sub-controls as switches only. The doorbell (bell state) and answer are not visible; securedDetails unused IntercomV2 (Gen 2) intercom/ → binary_sensor.py, switch.py, button, sensor, text partial No camera or two-way audio. Intercoms of a trust member and custom devices are skipped. Secured Intercoms and outputs get no entities. The output buttons send pulse, which is not documented for Intercom subcontrols, and are untested on hardware

docs.title: Not implemented
docs.text: AlarmChain, AlarmClock, LightController.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
Loxone's documents are not part of this repository. Download them from Loxone:

  • Structure File: format of LoxAPP3.json and the control types
  • Communicating with the Miniserver: commands, secured commands, events
  • Code: custom_components/loxone/

docs.title: pyloxone-api
docs.text:
The connection to the Miniserver is not part of this repository. It lives in the separate package pyloxone-api (PyPI), which handles:

  • the HTTP bootstrap (API key, structure file LoxAPP3.json, public key)
  • the WebSocket connection, encryption and token authentication
  • keepalive, token refresh, reconnect and backoff
  • encrypted and secured commands

The integration only consumes this package. Everything that talks to the Miniserver protocol belongs in pyloxone-api; everything that maps controls to Home Assistant entities belongs in custom_components/loxone/. The connection flow describes what the package does step by step.

docs.title: Version pinning
docs.text:
The version must be identical in two places:

File Used for custom_components/loxone/manifest.json (requirements) Home Assistant installs the package from here for users requirements.txt Development and tests

docs.title: Developing against a local checkout
docs.text:
To test changes in pyloxone-api together with the integration, clone it next to this repository:

Programmierung/
├── PyLoxone/
└── pyloxone-api/

./scripts/test installs a sibling checkout in editable mode. If its version equals the pin, the tests run against that local code; otherwise the pinned release from PyPI is used. Set PYLOXONE_API_SRC to a path that does not exist to always test against PyPI:

PYLOXONE_API_SRC=/nonexistent ./scripts/test

To run Home Assistant itself (the local runtime in .venv) against the checkout, use ./scripts/install-local-pyloxone-api. It installs the checkout as an editable package without changing Home Assistant's pinned dependencies.

docs.title: Token storage
docs.text: After a successful login the integration stores the Loxone token in its config entry (.storage/core.config_entries). The token is bound to host, port and user; a token for a different combination is ignored. See Token storage for the user-facing details.
